Regarding the LO case, with lower relative improvement, and where there is minimal lexical overlap, embedding-based approaches might also be well-suited since they are optimized for semantic similarity. The WikilinksNED Unseen-Mentions dataset was proposed in Onoe and Durrett ( 2020 ) . It is derived from the WikilinksNED dataset Eshel et al. ( 2017 ) , ensuring that the mention-entity pairs are unseen at test time. The examples in the dataset consist of single sentences, resulting in highly limited context. The target knowledge base is Wikipedia. We retrieve 64 candidates per mention through dense retrieval over Wikipedia entities, using the ELEVANT EL evaluation tool Bast et al. ( 2022 ) Wikipedia mappings 8 8 8 https://github.com/ad-freiburg/elevant/wiki/Mapping-Files#wikipedia-mappings , which achieves a recall of 83%. We also experiment with prior-based candidates using the candidate list from De Cao et al. ( 2021b ) , which yields a recall of 84%. Results reported in Table 7 show that BLINK leads on the benchmark. Regarding LELA, using the prior-based candidates leads to the best results. In particular, these candidates allow LELA to outperform the true zero-shot ET4EL, as well as the classical GENRE and ReFinED methods, which also use prior-based candidates. In fact, for all three models considered, using dense retrieval systematically underperforms on this benchmark.
